clue.text: Is mother after a cleaner personality?

indicators.note: the clue's first pieces are placed after the cleaner, so they follow it in the answer

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner employed to do housework
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether their mother, coming after the cleaner, is the household's real character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the clue's opening words behind the cleaner. A char is the British word for a hired cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is magnetic charm, the force of a striking personality.

clue.text: Repeatedly take part of skeleton

parts.note: to collar someone is to seize or arrest them, one way to take
to bone is slang for to steal, a second way to take

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep taking a piece of a skeleton, like a greedy anatomy student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' says two words for 'take' are needed in a row: COLLAR (seize) and BONE (pinch).
explanation.definitionFit: The clavicle, linking shoulder blade to breastbone, is one of the bones of the skeleton.

clue.text: Stern giant uncommonly stern

indicators.note: done in an uncommon way, so the letters of the two words before it are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A severe giant is stern to an unusual degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommonly' rearranges STERN GIANT; the final 'stern' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent words are harsh and severe, like a stern rebuke.

clue.text: One heading off for fireside

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word for one is taken off

parts.note: single means one, as in a single person

explanation.surface: A lone person heads off to sit by the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the S at the front of SINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a hearth or fire in a room, as in inglenook, the seat by the fireplace.

clue.text: The line of the dam?

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, so her line is descent traced through mothers, a female-led family system

explanation.surface: A question about the edge of a reservoir wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' suggests a barrier holding back water, but it is a mother, as in animal breeding; a line of descent through mothers is a matriarchal one.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarchate is a society ruled or traced through mothers, the line of the female parent.

clue.text: Sport reduced champion's calm

indicators.note: the word for sport is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to play is to sport, frolic or amuse oneself
El Cid was the Spanish champion and hero of medieval legend

explanation.surface: A sport, scaled back, is the calm a champion keeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the Y from PLAY; the champion is El Cid, the Castilian warrior known as 'the Champion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid describes a calm, untroubled temperament, quiet and peaceful.

clue.text: Those who bet are no experts

definitions.meaning: to lay a bet is to wager, so people who lay are those betting

explanation.definitionFit: Lay people are amateurs, not clergy or professionals; read as people who lay, they are gamblers placing wagers.

clue.text: One end of candid yarn

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'One end of candid yarn (4)' gives only C from candid; nothing gives ORD for CORD, so the clue looks cut short or misread by OCR, and no reprint was found.

clue.text: Course is sited in middle of Oldham

indicators.note: the small word is placed inside, sitting within the letters that follow
the central letters of the town name are taken

explanation.surface: A golf course or racecourse located in the heart of the Lancashire town of Oldham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the two central letters of the town, and 'sited in' puts the small word inside them. Oldham is a town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is a course of a meal, such as a main dish served at dinner.

clue.text: Inflamed crowd surrounding one-take action

indicators.note: the two pieces before it sit round the next one, enclosing it

parts.note: something lit is set alight, inflamed
the gate is the crowd attending a sports match
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An angry crowd surrounds a film shoot finished in a single take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' wraps LITGATE round I. GATE as the attendance at a football match is British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To litigate is to take legal action, going to court over a dispute.

clue.text: Limits to cursory power to American island

indicators.note: the limits of each of the next two words are their first and last letters

parts.note: US abbreviates the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: Limits to cursory power are handed to an American on some island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limits to' takes the first and last letters of both 'cursory' and 'power', giving C, Y, P and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is a Mediterranean island nation lying south of Turkey.

clue.text: Presumably not a slapdash play?

parts.note: a careless work would hardly be named after someone who takes care, so the title points to a Pinter drama about a janitor

explanation.surface: A theatre critic wonders whether a production was done carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Pinter's 1960 play is about a tramp taken on to look after a room; read literally, its title describes a person who takes care, the opposite of slapdash.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinter's play, named for a janitor, reads literally as a careful worker, unlike a slapdash one.

clue.text: Stay for hymn?

parts.note: a request to stay for a man, phrased in old language, which is also the title of a well-known Victorian hymn sung at funerals and the FA Cup final

explanation.surface: A request that someone remain until the singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for hymn' looks like 'to sing the hymn', but reads as 'for him': the old verb 'abide' means stay, and 'stay with me' is the hymn's own title in archaic form.
explanation.definitionFit: The hymn by Henry Lyte opens with a plea to the Lord to remain, its first line using the old verb for stay.

clue.text: Bird, female, engaged in wild shrieking

indicators.note: the single letter is engaged, or fitted, inside the other letters
wild suggests disorder, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A female bird is involved in some frantic screeching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges SHRIEKING, and 'engaged in' places F among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingfisher is a brightly coloured bird that dives for fish.

clue.text: Bent pins ruined-not pointed?

indicators.note: bent things are twisted out of shape, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bent pins are ruined and no longer sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' rearranges PINS RUINED. The definition plays on 'pointed' as sharp or witty: dull work lacks point.
explanation.definitionFit: Uninspired writing is dull and lacks sharpness, the opposite of pointed wit.

clue.text: Runs out of sparkling bay

indicators.note: the letter for runs is taken out of the word for sparkling

parts.note: bright means shining or sparkling
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs out of a sparkling bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R (runs, in cricket scoring) from BRIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bight is a wide curving bay or bend in a coastline.

clue.text: Description of sides, say, readily encountered?

definitions.meaning: a coin such as a penny has two faces, so its sides come at the rate of two per penny
something met everywhere is cheap and common

explanation.definitionFit: Two a penny is a British idiom for common or plentiful; literally it describes a coin's faces, two to each penny.

clue.text: Duke in formal party

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Duke in formal party (9)' has no D in RECEPTION and no wordplay for it; the clue looks garbled by OCR or cut short, and no reprint was found.

clue.text: Not that girl cuddling an individual? The very same

indicators.note: to cuddle is to hold close in an embrace, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: not that girl is 'not her'
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone protests that it was not that girl hugging some person, but the identical one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuddling' puts ONE inside NOT HER, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: None other is an emphatic phrase meaning exactly that person, the identical one.

clue.text: The Spanish start to gather in Scottish location

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: the start of the next word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The Spanish begin to gather in a place in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes G from 'gather'. Elgin is a town in Moray, north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a cathedral town in the Moray region of northern Scotland.

clue.text: Stomach chopped apricots as a snack

parts.note: a pot is a paunch or potbelly, a large stomach

indicators.note: chopped fruit is cut up, so the letters of the fruit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A belly full of chopped apricots, eaten as a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' rearranges the fruit's letters. A crisp is the British word for a potato chip.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato crisp is a thin fried slice of potato eaten from a bag as a snack.

clue.text: Upset copper placed to rise

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upward, so the word is reversed

parts.note: put means placed

explanation.surface: An agitated policeman is posted so that he goes up in rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' reads the word for placed upwards, which in a down answer means backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut up is an idiom for upset or distressed, as in being cut up about bad news.

clue.text: Extract of film hit

definitions.meaning: a short excerpt shown from a movie
to strike someone with a sharp blow

explanation.definitionFit: A clip is both a short excerpt from a film and a smart blow, as in a clip round the ear.

clue.text: Stone-operation needed for part of organ

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of fourteen pounds
op is short for a surgical operation

explanation.surface: A surgeon removes a stone from part of an organ in the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests a body part but is the musical instrument; ST is the British weight 'stone', fourteen pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is a knob on a pipe organ controlling a set of pipes.

clue.text: Recent section of Bible is hidden

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in the late news
NT is the New Testament, a section of the Bible

explanation.surface: A recently found passage of scripture lies hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent is present but concealed, not yet showing.

clue.text: Shock gutted one artist or another

indicators.note: a gutted word has its insides removed, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: another artist, one who makes engraved prints with acid

explanation.surface: Shocked and gutted, one painter turns on a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves SK from 'Shock'; 'another' (artist) gives ETCHER, so the clue names two kinds of artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketcher is an artist who makes quick rough drawings.

clue.text: Father retains a yard for fruit

indicators.note: the word for father keeps the next pieces within it

parts.note: papa is a child's word for father

explanation.surface: A father keeps a yard of land to grow fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retains' puts A and Y inside PAPA, before its final A.
explanation.definitionFit: The papaya is a tropical fruit with orange flesh, also called pawpaw.

clue.text: Power working again, but without one being ready

indicators.note: the letter for one is left out of the word before

parts.note: something repaired is mended and working again
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Power is restored, but with nobody ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes I (one) from REPAIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Prepared means ready, set up in advance for something.
